title: Medicare vs. Medicaid
summary: Explains how Medicare and Medicaid differ as government programs and how Dual Special Needs Plans serve people eligible for both.

atoms.title: Medicare vs. Medicaid at a glance
atoms.question: What is the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
atoms.text: Medicare and Medicaid are terms often heard together because both are government programs, but they work differently. Medicare is a national program run by the federal government, while Medicaid is managed by each state. People may qualify for Medicare, Medicaid or both, depending on their situation.
questions: What's the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?

atoms.title: What is Medicare?
atoms.question: What is Medicare?
atoms.text: Medicare is a national health insurance program run by the federal government. It covers people age 65 and older and some people under age 65 who may qualify due to a disability or another special situation. There are 4 different parts to Medicare, which helps give people more health care choices so they can pick the plan that best meets their needs.
questions: How many parts does Medicare have?

atoms.title: What is Medicaid?
atoms.question: What is Medicaid?
atoms.text: Medicaid is a way to get health care at a lower cost or sometimes at no cost to the person. It is managed by each state, so the eligibility requirements can change from state to state. A state may even have its own name for its Medicaid program.
questions: Do Medicaid rules differ by state?

atoms.title: What are Dual Special Needs Plans (D-SNP)?
atoms.question: What is a Dual Special Needs Plan?
atoms.text: Dual Special Needs Plans (D-SNP) are for people who could use some extra help, which may be because of income, disabilities, age and/or health conditions. Dual eligible health plans are a special type of Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) plan. Members keep all their Medicaid benefits, could get more benefits than with Original Medicare, and could get it all for a $0 plan premium.
questions: Can I have Medicare and Medicaid together?
Do dual eligible plans cost anything?

atoms.title: Can I be eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid?
atoms.question: Can I have both Medicare and Medicaid?
atoms.text: Yes, people may qualify for Medicare, Medicaid or both, depending on their situation. Dual Special Needs Plans include both Medicare and Medicaid benefits for those who are eligible for both.
questions: Can I get Medicare and Medicaid at the same time?

atoms.title: Medicaid is run by each state
atoms.question: Why do Medicaid requirements vary by state?
atoms.text: Medicaid is managed by each state, so the eligibility requirements can change from state to state. A state may also have its own name for its Medicaid program, so a program called something different locally may still be Medicaid.
questions: Why is Medicaid different in each state?
Does my state call Medicaid something else?

atoms.title: Short term insurance can fill a gap
atoms.question: What can fill a coverage gap while I wait for other coverage?
atoms.text: During times of transition, short term health insurance can help fill a gap in coverage from 1 month to just under 1 year, depending on the state. UnitedHealthcare notes that product design and availability vary by state.
questions: How long does short term insurance last?
Is short term insurance available in every state?
